tags.name: Wreck C-53
tags.qa_note: RE-AUDIT 2026-07-27 (deep wreck-history research): Cross-checked against Wikipedia (USS Scuffle AM-298; Felipe Santiago Xicotencatl bio) plus 4 dive/maritime sources. CONFLICTS FOUND AND PRESERVED IN TEXT (not silently resolved): (1) builder/location - Wikipedia says Winslow Marine Railway & Shipbuilding Co., Seattle WA; dive-tourism sources say 'Wilson Marine Shipworks,' Tampa FL - both stated, not reconciled. (2) Renaming to 'Felipe Xicotencatl C-53' occurred in 1994 per Wikipedia/Triton Diving, NOT at the 1962 transfer as previously stated - corrected. (3) Scuttling date - naval-history sources say sunk 1999/stricken 2000; dive sources say June 5, 2000 - both stated. (4) Depth reported inconsistently 10-24m across dive sources - range now noted. Tonnage: Wikipedia gives 650 long tons (660t) for the class, but no second independent source corroborates it for this specific hull, so per the 2-source rule it is OMITTED from the description rather than presented as confirmed. 'Named after a general under Santa Anna' claim flagged as disputed - Wikipedia's own bio calls him a colonel (posthumous honor) while the ship's official Mexican Navy name uses 'General'; both noted. Lingayen Gulf/Subic Bay WWII minesweep service INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED (Wikipedia + californiadiver.com, matching dates); a conflicting 'Gulf of Leyte' claim from another dive source was rejected as less-corroborated. Marine life pared to site-confirmed: black grouper (not 'Atlantic spotted grouper'), moray eels (general), glassy sweeper schools, nurse sharks (not 'juvenile reef sharks'), turtles (species unconfirmed). Removed unconfirmed silversides schooling and flamingo tongue cowries on deck fittings.
